title: Responder Preparedness Simulator and Rotation Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This document defines a compact, operationally focused playbook for responder preparedness: how we run on-call rotations, maintain high-quality runbooks, and validate readiness via a simulation (game-day) matrix. It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, and incident commanders who own model-serving, routing, and cache systems across Redwood Inference.

Scope:
- Applies to all production incidents impacting Redwood-hosted inference services (hosted API, Dedicated runtime pools, and Private control plane).
- Includes on-call rotation design, handover expectations, runbook hygiene, game-day exercises, status-page templates, and postmortem requirements.

Definitions
- Responder: the engineer assigned primary for a given service on a rotation.
- Bridge: a communication channel (Zoom/Google Meet + Slack) used for incident coordination.
- Severity levels: Sev1 (major outage), Sev2 (degradation with customer impact), Sev3 (minor impact / ticketable).

Key Principles
- SLO-first triage: incidents are prioritized by customer-facing SLO impact, not by metric noise.
- Fail-fast containment: aim to isolate faulty components quickly and restore partial service where possible.
- Evidence-driven postmortem: every Sev1/Sev2 requires a postmortem capturing root cause, timeline, and measurable action items.

Roles & Responsibilities
- Primary Responder: initial triage, bridge operator, first customer-facing status update (15–30 min).
- Secondary Responder: supports mitigation steps, runs verification, escalates to on-call lead if needed.
- On-call Lead (SRE staff): owns escalation decisions, exec comms, and long-running mitigation coordination.
- Pager / Customer Liaison (Customer Success): translates engineering status into customer-friendly updates.

Rotation Patterns and Rationale
1) Rotation structure: 1-week primary shifts with 48-hour secondary coverage for follow-up and weekend continuity.
2) Rationale: Longer weekly shifts reduce context switch overhead for constant systems work, while secondary coverage prevents knowledge gaps during handovers.
3) Follow-the-sun addendum: For regions with active customer bases in APAC, maintain a 2-person regional rotation to meet latency-sensitive support.
